title: Saint Alder's Rising Again
premise: When Saint Alder's founding patriarch, Ambrose Wren, is exhumed for a sesquicentennial ceremony, coroner Theo Sterling finds the coffin empty—and a fresh body buried in the founder's place. As Theo digs into town records, they discover the killer is someone inside the investigation itself, someone who has been editing the case file to steer suspicion outward while erasing their own connection to a decades-old disappearance. The trail leads to the Wren family's stolen inheritance and to Theo's own buried past in Saint Alder, forcing them to abandon the invisibility they've always hidden behind. At the anniversary dinner, Theo springs a trap using a falsified file entry, unmasking the town archivist—who is Ambrose's unrecognized descendant—as the killer, and finally claims their own place, and their own name, in the town they've served from the shadows.
about_author: Odile Sandoval is a former records clerk from a river town much like Saint Alder, where she spent years cataloguing the dead and the documents they left behind. Her fiction is known for its quiet, procedural menace and its fascination with the lies small towns tell to stay standing.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Theo Sterling, POV. Theo introduces their methodical life as Saint Alder's coroner, walking the cemetery and naming the dead. A summons arrives: the sesquicentennial committee has ordered Ambrose Wren's exhumation for a ceremonial reburial. Emotional beat: comfortable routine about to crack.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. At the exhumation, before the mayor and the Wren heirs, the coffin lid opens on nothing but ceremonial cloth—and beneath it, a recent corpse no one can identify. Theo seals the scene, noting one committee member watching too calmly. Emotional beat: professional calm masking a cold shock.

chapters.title: Chain of Custody
chapters.summary: Theo, POV, with a brief interlude from Deputy Marisol Vega. The body is logged, but the transfer paperwork contains an entry Theo doesn't remember writing. Someone has touched the file. Emotional beat: first vertigo of distrust.

chapters.title: The Wren Inheritance
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo interviews the Wren descendants at Wrenwood House and learns the estate's terms: the founder's remains must lie in state for the anniversary or the trust dissolves. The corpse in the coffin threatens everyone's money. Emotional beat: motive blooming everywhere.

chapters.title: A Name No One Knows
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. The unidentified body resists identification—fingerprints burned, teeth pulled. Theo recognizes the surgical precision of someone who knew exactly what a coroner would check. Emotional beat: the killer is one of us.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Kindness
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Town archivist Edmund Hale helpfully produces century-old burial records, including an 1898 gap Theo finds suspicious. Hale's warmth is disarming; Theo notes it and moves on. Emotional beat: the reader's first look at the killer hiding in plain sight.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Marisol Vega, POV. Marisol dredges county records and finds a 1974 drowning ruled accidental by Theo's predecessor—a girl from the Wren household staff, never claimed. Emotional beat: the past has a body count.

chapters.title: Theo's Own File
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Someone leaves a copy of Theo's adoption records on their desk, hinting Theo's arrival in Saint Alder was no accident. Emotional beat: invisibility revoked; the hunter is being hunted.

chapters.title: Second Exhumation
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo quietly exhumes the 1974 girl and finds her coffin also disturbed—same tool marks, same careful hand. The killer has been practicing for decades. Emotional beat: dread deepens into pattern.

chapters.title: The Heir Who Left
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. A Wren cousin, long estranged, returns to town and becomes the obvious suspect: he had access, motive, and a temper. The town wants him guilty. Emotional beat: Theo resists the easy answer.

chapters.title: Tampering
chapters.summary: Marisol, POV. Marisol discovers the case file's digital audit trail has been scrubbed—by someone with municipal credentials. Only a handful of people could do it. Emotional beat: the circle tightens.

chapters.title: Anniversary Approaches
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Preparations for the sesquicentennial dinner accelerate; the trust's lawyers give Theo nine days to produce Ambrose's remains or the estate liquidates. Emotional beat: the clock becomes a character.

chapters.title: The Estranged Cousin Dies
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. The obvious suspect is found dead in Wrenwood's boathouse, staged to look like suicide, a confession typed and signed. Theo knows the signature was traced. Emotional beat: grief and fury—the killer is cleaning house.

chapters.title: Reading the Killer's Hand
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Studying the forged confession, Theo realizes its author knows coroner procedure intimately—knew Theo would check the paper, not the pen. The killer is building a file Theo will believe. Emotional beat: grim respect for the adversary.

chapters.title: The 1898 Gap
chapters.summary: Marisol, POV. Marisol reconstructs the missing 1898 records from a private diary: a Wren bastard child, erased from the family line, raised by household staff. The drowned girl of 1974 was that line's last keeper. Emotional beat: inheritance as wound.

chapters.title: Where Ambrose Actually Went
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo traces the founder's true remains to an unmarked plot the archivist's office catalogued decades ago—meaning whoever moved them had keys, access, and time across generations. Emotional beat: the shape of the answer, not yet the face.

chapters.title: A Trap in the File
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo plants a fabricated entry in the case file—a false lead about evidence hidden in the cemetery's oldest crypt—and tells only the inner circle. Emotional beat: the invisible coroner finally sets a snare.

chapters.title: Night in the Crypt
chapters.summary: Theo and Marisol, alternating POV. On the anniversary eve, someone enters the crypt and is caught: Edmund Hale, the archivist—descendant of the erased Wren line, who moved the founder's bones years ago to expose the trust's fraud, and killed to keep his claim from being buried again. Emotional beat: confrontation, confession, and a desperate flight.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. With Hale in custody, Theo must still stand before the town at the dinner, produce the founder's remains, and name the fraud the Wren trust was built on. Emotional beat: public reckoning; Theo chooses visibility.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Ambrose Wren is laid to rest properly, and the drowned girl of 1974 is buried beside him with her true name read aloud. The town's founding story is rewritten in the open. Emotional beat: mourning made honest.

chapters.title: The Coroner's Ledger
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo closes the case file, adds their own adoption records to the town archive voluntarily, and signs their original name for the first time. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed on one's own terms.

chapters.title: What Saint Alder Owes
chapters.summary: Theo and Marisol, closing POV. Weeks later, the trust is redistributed, Wrenwood becomes a public archive under Marisol's oversight, and Theo walks the cemetery again—every grave by name, including two new ones. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace with a watchful horizon.
